reason: While the text depicts Yahweh as physically remote and all-powerful, it explicitly contradicts the characterization of being 'emotionally removed.' God uses intimate language—'I have borne you on eagles' wings and brought you to me' (Exodus 19:4)—expressing tender care. God actively establishes a covenant relationship, demonstrates emotional responsiveness (anger at the golden calf incident, Exodus 32:7-10), and responds to Moses' intercession. God directly communicates concerns and desires for relationship with the people. The narrative shows God as emotionally invested in the covenant and responsive to human prayer, not emotionally detached.
